text:
jin_cove: Hi team — getting ready to onboard CoveBank with BYOK. We have an AWS CMK in our account (arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/abcd-1234-efgh). Questions: 1) What exact RBAC/grant do you need so Redwood can do envelope encrypt/decrypt in our account? 2) We need CloudTrail/audit events that include envelope metadata so our SIEM can map activity to tenant ids. 3) We rotate keys every 90 days, can Redwood handle automated rewraps or do we need to orchestrate? Thanks.

jess_support: Thanks @jin_cove — quick answers up front: we support cross-account grants on AWS (preferred) and Azure Key Vault + GCP KMS via service accounts. We do not import customer CMKs into our HSMs. Can you confirm the KMS provider and whether you want Redwood to assume a role in your account or use a grant? Also OK to share the key ARN masked.

jin_cove: AWS — account 111222333444, key arn above. Prefer cross-account grant. For audit: we want each envelope operation to include tenant_id + route + request_id in the log so our SIEM can correlate. Is that possible?

alex_sec: @jess_support + @jin_cove — recommend using a CreateGrant with GranteePrincipal set to our role arn (we'll provide exact). Required KMS operations: kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey. Example create-grant command:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/abcd-1234-efgh --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/redwood-kms-proxy --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey DescribeKey
```
Also please use an EncryptionContext with {"tenant_id":"<TENANT>","route":"<ROUTE>"} — we log that context on our side and include it in an envelope_metadata field we surface to audit logs when possible.

pat_infra: For IAM/trust: ensure the redwood role can be assumed or referenced and that the key policy explicitly allows the role. Minimal key policy snippet to attach:
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowRedwoodProxy",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/redwood-kms-proxy" },
  "Action": [ "kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:DescribeKey" ],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
Note: prefer fine-grained grants over wide key policies for cross-account setups.

jess_support: Quick doc gap we found: the exact EncryptionContext keys we expect. For onboarding we require: tenant_id, route (string), request_id (uuid), and model_id (optional). We'll add this to the KB. Quick validation you can run locally:
```
aws kms generate-data-key --key-id <KEY_ARN> --key-spec AES_256 --encryption-context '{"tenant_id":"test-tenant"}'
```
If that returns AccessDenied it's an RBAC/grant issue.

jin_cove: Ran the generate-data-key command — got AccessDenied: NotAuthorized to perform kms:GenerateDataKey on resource. Short stack: AccessDenied.

alex_sec: That's consistent with no grant/policy mapping. Please add the grant or update key policy to include the redwood principal. If you want, share the key alias and we can run a permission check from our side (we won't store key material). Regarding rotation: when you rotate the CMK we support an automated rewrap flow — we update the envelope header with wrap_key_id and wrap_key_version and can coordinate a short cutover window (typical 24h). If you prefer a manual rollover we can provide scripts. We also recommend emitting the encryption context in CloudTrail so your SIEM can tie operations to tenant ids.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5894 — Security onboarding + BYOK validation for CoveBank. Assigned to jess_support, alex_sec. :white_check_mark:

jess_support: Next steps for @jin_cove: 1) Create grant or update key policy using the snippets above; 2) run the generate-data-key test again; 3) share a CloudTrail sample event for a failed call if any. I'll schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to finish RBAC and rotation plan. Thanks! :thumbsup:
